claims.text: The baseline is a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy without molybdenum.
The baseline alloy has a relatively homogeneous microstructure.
The intervention adds approximately 5 at% Mo while adjusting the other elements to remain within 5–35 at% each.
Adding approximately 5 at% Mo will promote in situ formation of Mo-rich precipitates or nanoscale segregations.
The Mo-rich precipitates or segregations will be fine and evenly distributed at grain boundaries.
Mo-rich grain-boundary precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
Mo-rich grain-boundary precipitates will inhibit grain-boundary sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion and inhibited grain-boundary sliding will reduce the elevated-temperature creep rate.
Impeded dislocation motion and inhibited grain-boundary sliding will increase elevated-temperature yield strength.
The Mo-modified alloy will have a lower creep rate than the otherwise comparable Mo-free alloy at elevated temperature.
The Mo-modified alloy will have a higher yield strength than the otherwise comparable Mo-free alloy at elevated temperature.
The proposed operating window for assessing the intervention is 700–900°C.
The test comparison should use identical thermomechanical processing and creep testing at 800°C under constant applied load.
The stability and distribution of Mo-rich precipitates in a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy are unverified.
The magnitude of mechanical improvement may depend on processing details and phase evolution.
